rationale.usefulness: Queryable component contracts, templates, themes, version-bearing responses and source ejection address a concrete recurring problem in agent-built React interfaces. The report gives useful adoption checks for React 19, CSS order, scoped package selection and generated instruction files, plus realistic classroom, review-queue and media-board pilots with observable outcomes.
rationale.impact: An inspectable common design reference can meaningfully improve a defined part of AI-assisted frontend development. Its significance is domain-specific: the evidence does not show measured agent productivity, general intelligence gains or broad adoption outside the publisher's claimed internal history.
rationale.novelty: Designing the CLI, typed machine responses, discovery manifest and human documentation as a shared agent-facing interface is a meaningful distinction. Components, theming and source customization themselves are established practices, and comparative superiority has not been demonstrated.
rationale.maturity: The public repository and detailed Core/CLI guides document substantial implementation and maintenance tooling. However, the project remains beta, requires React 19+, leaves Lab unpublished and charts canary-only, and has not been installed or tested in this assessment. Internal scale claims cannot certify public-package reliability or accessibility.
rationale.openness: The actual MIT license permits inspection, modification and redistribution with notice retention, and public source, exported internals and swizzle make local ownership and portability unusually strong. External dependencies retain their own terms and the unpublished internal Lab limits complete reproduction of the internal system, so the score is below the maximum.
